issues.t: Second gear can overheat and break
issues.sym: Slipping, a flashing D indicator, harsh shifts, or the transmission suddenly locking up while driving.
issues.why: Second gear in this automatic did not get enough oil and could overheat until it broke. Honda recalled these years to fix it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the open recall. If the transmission slips or locks, stop driving and have it towed in.

issues.t: Blinking D light from pressure switch or shift faults
issues.sym: The D indicator on the dash blinks, the check-engine light comes on, or shifts become rough or delayed.
issues.why: Owners commonly trace this to a failing transmission pressure switch or shift solenoid, and some of these transmissions go on to fail outright.
issues.next: Have the codes read soon. Replacing a pressure switch or solenoid early and keeping the fluid fresh can prevent bigger damage.

issues.t: Timing belt may rub a bolt and fail
issues.sym: Possibly a rubbing or slapping noise from the front of the engine, then a sudden stall with no restart.
issues.why: On some early builds a bolt could contact the timing belt and wear through it. Honda recalled the affected vehicles.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. A broken timing belt on this engine can cause serious internal damage, so do not keep driving if you hear new noises from the belt area.

issues.t: Passenger air bag inflator can rupture (do not drive)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. The danger only shows up in a crash.
issues.why: The 2003 Pilot uses a high-risk passenger inflator that can rupture and throw metal pieces. Honda told owners of unrepaired vehicles not to drive them.
issues.next: Do not drive the vehicle until the free repair is done. Check the VIN and ask a dealer about towing or mobile repair.

issues.t: Key can come out when not in Park
issues.sym: The ignition key can be removed even though the shifter is not in Park, so the vehicle may roll after you walk away.
issues.why: The ignition interlock that is supposed to hold the key until the shifter is in Park could wear and stop working.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check the recall status by VIN until the interlock is repaired.

issues.t: Headlight wiring can overheat and dim the low beams
issues.sym: Low beam headlights dim, flicker, or go out, and the connector may look melted.
issues.why: Terminals in the headlight wiring could overheat and melt, cutting power to the low beams.
issues.next: Check for the recall and have the harness repaired. Avoid driving at night with dim or failed headlights.

issues.t: Stability control may brake on its own
issues.sym: The vehicle brakes suddenly or pulls without you pressing the pedal, sometimes with a VSA warning light.
issues.why: A fault in the stability and traction control module could command braking when it was not needed. Honda recalled affected 2005 models.
issues.next: Have the recall done right away. If it happens, pull over safely and have the vehicle checked before driving further.

issues.t: Steering column may be assembled wrong
issues.sym: Loose, clunky, or unusual steering feel.
issues.why: Some steering columns were assembled incorrectly at the factory and could affect steering control. Honda recalled the affected vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the steering inspected before relying on the vehicle.

issues.t: Fuel tank may leak
issues.sym: A gasoline smell around the vehicle or drips under the rear.
issues.why: Some fuel tanks were made incorrectly and could leak fuel, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, do not drive and keep it away from ignition sources. Check the VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Cylinder shutoff vibration, oil use and misfires
issues.sym: Vibration or shudder while cruising when the ECO light is on, needing to add oil between changes, or a check-engine light with misfire codes.
issues.why: The system that turns off cylinders to save fuel causes vibration on some engines and is linked by owners to oil burning, fouled spark plugs and stuck piston rings.
issues.next: Check the oil by dipstick between changes. Have misfires diagnosed and ask a dealer about updates or piston ring repairs if oil use is high.

issues.t: Lower control arm bushings wear out early
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, a vague or wandering feel, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The rubber compliance bushings in the lower control arms tear or crack early. Honda extended warranty coverage for them.
issues.next: Have the bushings inspected and ask a dealer whether the extended coverage still applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Driver air bag may be missing rivets
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see. The problem may only show in a crash.
issues.why: Some driver air bag modules were built without all of their rivets, which can affect how the air bag deploys.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the air bag module repaired.

issues.t: Rear damper bolts or spindle nuts may be loose
issues.sym: Clunking or rattling from the rear, or a loose, unstable feel.
issues.why: Some vehicles left the factory with rear damper bracket bolts or spindle nuts not tightened properly.
issues.next: Have the recall inspection done before driving much further. A loose rear suspension can affect control.

issues.t: Fuel tank vent valve may leak
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell, especially after filling up.
issues.why: The case of a fuel tank vent valve could crack or leak fuel, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Do not ignore a fuel smell. Park away from buildings and get the recall done.

issues.t: Pistons may wear and fail
issues.sym: Engine knocking, rough running, a check-engine light, or loss of power.
issues.why: Some engines were built with pistons that could wear too fast and fail. Honda recalled affected 2013 models.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. If the engine knocks or runs rough, stop driving and have it inspected.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, will not start, or stalls while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank can fail and cut fuel to the engine. Honda recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open fuel pump recalls and have the pump replaced. If the engine stalls, get it towed rather than restarting repeatedly.

issues.t: Fuel injector misfires
issues.sym: A check-engine light, misfire codes, hesitation or bucking when accelerating, and worse fuel economy.
issues.why: Honda found some injectors were installed wrong at the factory or affected by contamination, which upsets fuel flow and causes misfires.
issues.next: Have the misfire diagnosed and ask the dealer about Honda bulletin 18-025 for your VIN.

issues.t: Shudder between 20 and 60 mph
issues.sym: A light shudder or vibration while cruising at moderate speeds, like driving over rumble strips.
issues.why: The torque converter lockup clutch can judder. Honda says the converter itself is usually not faulty and the judder does not harm the transmission.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about Honda bulletin 17-015 and any software update before agreeing to a torque converter replacement.

issues.t: Connecting rod bearing can wear and seize
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, rough running, a check-engine light, stalling, or the engine locking up.
issues.why: A manufacturing error with the crankshaft can make the rod bearings wear out early. Honda recalled some years and federal safety regulators are probing more engine failures.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. If the engine knocks, stop driving and have it towed in.

issues.t: Engine may not restart after Auto Idle Stop
issues.sym: The engine shuts off at a stop as designed but does not restart when you lift off the brake.
issues.why: Honda bulletins call for a fuel injection software update, and if that fails, new starter parts and a valve adjustment. Federal regulators opened investigations into the problem.
issues.next: Turn off Auto Idle Stop with its button until the dealer applies bulletins 23-008 or 23-009.

issues.t: Fuel tank welds may leak
issues.sym: A fuel smell or wet spots under the vehicle near the tank.
issues.why: Welds on some fuel tanks could separate and let fuel leak, which is a fire risk. Honda issued two recalls on 2016 tanks.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and check the VIN for both recalls.

issues.t: Hood may fly open while driving
issues.sym: The hood is hard to latch, rattles, or pops up at speed.
issues.why: The hood latch striker can corrode or fail, so the hood may open while driving and block the view.
issues.next: Get the recall done. Until then, check that the hood is fully latched before every drive.

issues.t: Timing belt teeth may separate
issues.sym: A slapping or grinding noise from the engine front, then a stall with no restart.
issues.why: Teeth on some timing belts could come off, letting the belt skip or break. Honda recalled the affected vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. Stop driving if you hear new noises from the timing belt area.

issues.t: Rear subframe can rust at the suspension mounts
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear over bumps, a loose rear end, or odd handling, especially in salt-belt states.
issues.why: The rear subframe can corrode where the suspension attaches, which may let a suspension part separate.
issues.next: Have the rear subframe inspected under the recall, sooner if you hear clunks.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor fault may fire the air bag
issues.sym: An air bag warning light, or the passenger air bag status light acting oddly.
issues.why: The weight sensor in the front passenger seat can short out, which can cause the air bag to deploy without a crash or not work right.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both recalls and have the sensor replaced. Get it checked promptly if the air bag light is on.

issues.t: Backup camera image delayed or missing
issues.sym: The rear camera screen stays blank, freezes, or shows up late when backing up.
issues.why: Software errors and a faulty camera cable connector can stop or delay the image. Honda issued several recalls.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open camera recalls and look over your shoulder when reversing until fixed.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder may separate from booster
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, longer stopping distances, or a brake warning light.
issues.why: The brake master cylinder could come loose from the brake booster, reducing braking.
issues.next: Do not drive if the brake pedal feels wrong. Check the VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Engine computer software can cause stalls
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, rough running, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: A programming error in the engine control computer can make the engine lose power or stall.
issues.next: Get the free software update. If power drops, move to a safe spot and do not keep driving.

issues.t: Loose steel ball in steering gear
issues.sym: Clicking or grinding when steering, or steering that feels notchy or stiff.
issues.why: A loose ball bearing from manufacturing can end up inside the steering gear and interfere with steering.
issues.next: Have the recall inspection done right away and avoid driving if steering feels wrong.

issues.t: Fuel filler neck tube may separate
issues.sym: A fuel smell or leak near the fuel door, especially after filling up.
issues.why: A tube in the fuel filler neck can come apart and leak fuel, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, do not drive. Check the VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Brake pedal pivot pin may come loose
issues.sym: A loose, rattling, or unresponsive brake pedal.
issues.why: The pin the brake pedal pivots on may not be secured and could fall out, cutting brake pedal function.
issues.next: Do not drive if the pedal feels loose. Have the recall inspection done right away.

issues.t: Driver seat cushion frame may be loose
issues.sym: The driver seat shifts, rocks, or creaks when you sit down or brake.
issues.why: The frame under the driver's seat cushion may not be secured properly, which can affect protection in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recalls and have the seat inspected.

issues.t: Third-row seat belt may be trapped
issues.sym: A third-row seat belt cannot be pulled out or buckled.
issues.why: The belt can get caught behind a trim panel, so a passenger may not be able to buckle up.
issues.next: Do not seat anyone in a third-row spot whose belt does not work. Get the recall repair.

issues.t: Rear subframe bolts may be loose
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear or a loose, unstable feel.
issues.why: Bolts holding the rear subframe may not have been tightened properly at the factory.
issues.next: Have the recall inspection done before regular driving.

issues.t: Power window stops working
issues.sym: A window will not go up or down, or it moves slowly and crookedly with a grinding sound.
issues.why: The window motor and regulator assembly wears out, usually well into the car’s life, and it is one of the most reported electrical faults on these years.
issues.next: Have the regulator and motor replaced. Leave the window up until then so rain and thieves stay out.

issues.t: Air conditioning blows warm air
issues.sym: The air from the vents turns warm, sometimes only on one side or only at idle.
issues.why: The compressor and its electrical relay are common failures on these years, and a failed compressor can send debris through the system.
issues.next: Get it diagnosed before adding refrigerant. A compressor that has come apart means flushing the lines and replacing the dryer too.
